clusters.name: Jonah leaving for the conservatory, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around September 1991 when Jonah began at Wexley Conservatory: a wrist injury in October stopped his playing, his anxiety rose and functioning fell; he and Rafe clashed and Rafe moved out in November; by January 1992 he was lost and low with his grandfather gone and his mother about to remarry. His grandfather Gordon died in June 1991, and his stepmother Bettina separated from his father in 1987 over a baby, which they later had as Tara in July 1990. The shifts pile up around the conservatory start and the injury, with Rafe's move and his grandfather's death months before; the period settles by spring when he earned money fixing radios.

clusters.name: Jonah's father Clifford's return and the family rebuilding, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around January 1989 when Jonah's grandfather Clifford came back into the family after years away: within months, in April 1989, Desmond took a rental on Quarry Lane while the Hollin Road house was rebuilt; by September 1989 Jonah settled there with his mother and Desmond, in a loud and cramped household with Desmond's two children. His sleep troubles began that autumn, and he dropped chess and debate club. His sister Tara was born in July 1990. From September 1991 onward came the conservatory, the wrist injury, Rafe's conflict, and the loss of his grandfather Gordon in June 1991. His grandmother Winifred had thyroid surgery around 1992. By early 1994 he felt stung that his father had never heard of his film, and he found his drive again through an exchange in Portugal. The shifts pile up in clusters from 1989 onward, with the household changes and his own troubles mounting through secondary school and the conservatory start; the period settles as his degree work caught hold.
clusters.change: Merged r1 and r2; the opening event is Clifford's return in 1989, which brought the household changes that set the larger arc in motion.

clusters.name: Jonah's move away and the long slump, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around September 2001 Jonah began running out of steam for performing and his anxiety rose; his grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002. In early 2002 he had a disastrous audition and was done with performing; by September 2002 he was on poor terms with family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour. In January 2003 he met Marisol; he moved to Fenwick in June to live with her, then separated by October and sank into a deep depression back in Thornbury by November. His grandmother spent her final months in his parents' home in the autumn of 2003. He could not face his family, relied on friends Corbin, Dale, and Hamish, and his functioning fell sharply. By January 2004 he began swimming and returned to his therapist Victor Halloran; his functioning came back up. His grandmother Winifred died in February 2004. The shifts pile up from 2001 through 2004 around his burnout, the failed audition, the brief relationship, and the depression that followed; his grandmother's illness and death sit within this span but are secondary to his own crisis. The period settles as therapy and swimming began to lift him.

clusters.name: Jonah's grandmother Lorna's death and his move to nursing school, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: In January 2008 Jonah's grandmother Lorna died; Clifford's death is also noted around then, the year uncertain. In July 2008 Jonah was at Alder Creek building with Silas and was too drained for conversation with his mother; she pressed to visit him despite his repeated refusals, and when she came they clashed and she never got inside. In August 2008 he left for nursing school in Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to his mother, a cutoff that held for roughly a year. His aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation. Bree's older child was born in August 2010. The shifts pile up around Jonah's move to nursing school and the cutoff with his mother; his grandmother's death opens the period but sits with other family losses, and his aunt's stroke falls in the quiet months after his move. The period settles as the silence began to ease and he found his footing in nursing.

clusters.name: Jonah's marriage to Wren and his partner's family involvement, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: In March 2017 Jonah married Wren; he saw his mother a bit less once Wren came along. His partner Wren's cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017. His sister Tara married James, flying for a regional airline in Rennick. In October 2019 Wren's mother Frances retired; Wren became swamped with a street party, a fundraiser, and the drive to the lake for the retirement weekend. Jonah responded by overfunctioning, laying out a strict plan to settle her. Wren talks with her father Hugo and brother Leo all day, and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear—a tight fusion. At the lake weekend in late October, Jonah was awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as others rose; Wren became anxious when he had no sleep at family occasions. His anxiety around her family is at its worst; he feels he doesn't belong. His sister Tara expected a baby, Russell's first grandchild that Jonah knows of. The shifts pile up in late October 2019 around Wren's swamped state, her family's tight fusion, and Jonah's sleep failure at the family occasion. The period settles after the weekend with the plan in place and the dinner done, though the tension between them about his sleeplessness and his overfunctioning remains.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
